headline: Kai, the war premium is back: oil up 4% on Pentagon strike reports, futures lower, and the 10-year just off its 24-year high.
subline: The Fed's minutes point to one more hike this year, PepsiCo opens the Q3 earnings season this morning, and jobless claims land at 8:30 ET.
asof: Pre-market · as of ~6:35 AM ET, futures and quotes from a ~6 AM board · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Ten-year touches 5.35%, a 24-year high
items.sentence: The 10-year hit 5.35% on Wednesday, up more than 60 basis points since late July, as investors demand a higher premium for inflation and fiscal risk, per FXStreet.

items.title: Fed minutes point to one more hike this year
items.sentence: September's minutes show a committee that expects another hike before year-end but is keeping an open mind between October 28 and December 9, per TheStreet, which put Wednesday's S&P 500 close at 7,801.77.

items.title: Oil jumps 4% as Gulf shipping comes under fire
items.sentence: WTI rose above $91 after fresh attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, eight months into the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, per Yahoo Finance's morning board, the source for the strip above.

items.title: PepsiCo opens a Q3 season priced for 29.5% growth
items.sentence: PepsiCo reports this morning to start a season FactSet pegs at 29.5% S&P 500 earnings growth, with tech seen up 65%, per Schwab's market update.

items.title: Bitcoin slips toward $83,000 as yields bite
items.sentence: Bitcoin traded near $82,900 early Thursday, down 1.8% on the day, after more than $500 million in long liquidations and roughly $213 million of crypto-ETF outflows Wednesday, per Analytics Insight — competition from a 5%-plus Treasury is the stated culprit.

items.title: Pentagon reportedly drafting strikes on Iran nuclear, energy sites
items.sentence: Benzinga reports the Pentagon is preparing options against Iranian nuclear and energy targets while a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker burns in the Gulf of Oman and Tehran insists Hormuz stays shut.

items.title: Hurricane Isaias takes aim at the Gulf Coast
items.sentence: The season's first Atlantic hurricane carries warnings from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Florida Panhandle ahead of a Friday-night landfall at Category 1 or 2 strength, per The Weather Channel.

items.title: Nobel week: the literature prize lands this morning
items.sentence: The Swedish Academy names its literature laureate today, after Wednesday's chemistry prize went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for asymmetric autocatalysis, per Britannica.

items.title: New super PAC will spend against AI-backed candidates
items.sentence: The Guardrails Alliance plans $1.2 million to oppose midterm candidates aligned with the AI industry, demanding independent oversight with real enforcement power, per Fox News.

items.title: Microsoft rebuilds Windows around AI agents
items.sentence: Satya Nadella pitched Windows as 'hybrid intelligence' that runs Copilot locally on-device, alongside a $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra on Nvidia's RTX Spark chip due October 16, per Fortune.

items.title: SpaceX seeks $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips
items.sentence: Reuters confirms an FT report that Apollo would lead roughly $10 billion in bank loans plus $30 billion of investment-grade debt tied to xAI's Colossus 2 build-out, with SPCX shares off about 2% on the news.

items.title: OpenAI model posts proofs of unsolved math problems
items.sentence: OpenAI says an internal frontier model worked through hundreds of open problems at about three hours apiece and published the proofs to a public GitHub repository, per Fox News.

items.title: OpenAI retakes model-traffic share from Anthropic
items.sentence: OpenRouter data seen by the Wall Street Journal puts OpenAI near 50% of routed usage, up from under 25% in January, per Gizmodo, which cautions the sample skews toward AI-native startups.
